adaptations.withheld: sacred or restricted dance: no teaching adaptations

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Graceful wrist circles, hand waves, finger snapping; waving scarves or small props in some styles
movement_profile.difficulty: beginner to advanced depending on style
movement_profile.footwork: Basic 6-count step patterns in chain dances; rhythmic footwork in war dances; delicate wrist and hand circles in solo improvisation
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Circle or line formations for chain dances; solo space for improvisation; paired or small group formations in combat dances
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Soft undulations in solo and ritual dances; more restrained in court dances
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Mostly low to moderate levels; jumps not commonly described
movement_profile.partnering: Limited in most dances; social dances may have paired improvisation without physical contact
movement_profile.posture: Upright with controlled torso; expressive facial gestures especially in solo dances

signature_moves.description: Delicate circular movements of the wrists emphasizing grace
signature_moves.name: Wrist Circles

signature_moves.description: Flowing hand gestures resembling fishermen’s cooperative movements in Bandari dance
signature_moves.name: Hand Waves

signature_moves.description: Sharp finger snaps used in Bojnordi dance
signature_moves.name: Finger Snapping (Peshkan)

signature_moves.description: Rhythmic stick movements in combat or social stick dances
signature_moves.name: Stick Play (Choob Bazi)

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Varies by style; generally moderate with rhythmic accents; some dances accelerate to fast tempos
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid imitating sacred trance dances without initiation; avoid mixed-gender contact in public settings due to cultural restrictions

music_profile.musical_form: Music closely follows dance rhythms with repetitive melodic cycles
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Cyclical rhythmic patterns emphasizing melody and dance steps; shir-e mâdar rhythm
music_profile.sound_description: Music features cyclical 6/8 rhythms with melodic ornamentation, supporting both communal and solo dance forms; vocal chanting or singing may accompany ritual or court dances.
music_profile.vocal_style: Includes chanting in ritual dances and expressive singing in court and social dances

basic_steps: Form a circle or line holding hands or waists for chain dances
Step right, step left, step right, lift left foot, step left, lift right foot (6-count pattern)
Use wrist circles and delicate hand gestures for solo improvisational dances
In war dances, practice rhythmic footwork and stick movements
For ritual dances, follow chanting rhythm and controlled body undulations
teaching.formation: Chain dances use circle or line formations; solo dances performed individually; war dances often in pairs or small groups; ritual dances may be performed in circles or individually
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with basic foot patterns and hand gestures; intermediate dancers add improvisation and expressive facial movements; advanced dancers master complex rhythms and trance techniques
teaching.rhythm: Commonly 6/8 meter (shir-e mâdar) with rhythmic accents matching melody; some styles use 7/8 variations
